title: 2nd week of trading with GPT+Kimi
author: ARWorlds_umut
selftext: I starrted my trading journey 2 weeks ago. I know nothing about the stock market. I gave 5k to my AI agents, I'm trying to build a trading deck with a feedback loop. This week I'm quite happy with the results.

comments.author: Ill-Satisfaction350
comments.body: Do u mind sharing how u build that loop and is kimi running on ur local ?

replies.author: ARWorlds_umut
replies.body: Everything is local, I'm just talking to codex and kimicli. It mostly consists of me asking them to do trades during the day. And after the trading session is over I ask what mistakes/errors/bugs we encountered and spend some of my quota asking what tooling/skills/strategy we can build.

replies.author: leppardfan
replies.body: How are you feeding the LLM data...a spread sheet(s) full of technical analysis and stock price values? Is there an MCP involved? What does the prompt ask the LLM to do with that data?

replies.author: ARWorlds_umut
replies.body: I answered below what I do but there really is nothing special. I'm just talking to AI coding agents and asking them to build tooling and strategies on the alpaca api. Then I run them during the day. Honestly, I wasn't expecting them to do so well with zero knowledge from my side.

comments.author: lil_pepper09
comments.body: Is this agentic trading? If so, how often do your agents scan the market throughout the trading day, and how token-intensive is it? I use Claude and am trying to determine how practical it would be to run something similar. I’d also love to know how you structured the prompts, tools, and feedback loop, if you’re willing to share.

replies.author: d3xinho
replies.body:
Personally mine gets triggered by technical indicators (EMA, FVG, ICT, etc...) so it uses less credits and if the strat is TA heavy it's very convenient.

For fundamental stats typically 4 times a day.

replies.author: lil_pepper09
replies.body: Does your agent scan for technical setups only four times a day, or does a separate program continuously monitor the indicators and trigger the agent whenever conditions are met? Also, how frequently is it checking for EMA, FVG, and ICT setups?

replies.author: d3xinho
replies.body:
It scans macro conditions 4 times a day for fundamental trading, news, etc... 

separate strategies from the indicator ones.

Indicator ones only get triggered on events, so only if RSI crosses below 30 on 1h, EMA 12 crosses 26 or FVG formed a bullish Gap, etc..
If these events don't happen in a couple of days, I'm spending no credits.

replies.author: lil_pepper09
replies.body: That makes sense. What system continuously monitors those indicators and sends the event to your agent? For example, are you using TradingView webhooks, a Python script connected to market data, or something else? When the event triggers, what information and prompt get sent to the agent?

replies.author: d3xinho
replies.body: Its a websocket/daemons connected to Hyperliquid. I mean, I know the system works like that, if you're asking what I am using, it's Cod3x, app.cod3x.org

comments.author: Elite-human
comments.body:
I get what you're doing. From what I understand, you're using an LLM and it's giving you buy and sell suggestions, right?

If that's correct, could you tell me what prompt you're feeding it? I'm curious about how you're structuring the prompt to get those trade recommendations.

replies.author: Ok-Original4933
replies.body: tho k it’s agentic trading he’s not asking the llm it’s doing it automatically

replies.author: Elite-human
replies.body:
That raises another question. What data is the agent being fed to produce these kinds of outputs?

So it's not like you're manually asking the LLM for buy or sell signals. It's making those decisions automatically. I'm more interested in understanding what market data, indicators, price action, order flow, or other inputs the agent receives before it generates a trade.

replies.author: TheImperfectAlgo
replies.body: That’s exactly the right question. I think the prompt is actually one of the least important parts. The quality of the inputs matters much more. If I were building it, I’d feed structured OHLCV data, indicator values, higher-timeframe context, open positions, account/risk state, and market session info. Then I’d have deterministic code validate any trade before it reaches execution. An LLM shouldn’t be making decisions from a screenshot of a chart.
